scope: Primary-source audit of multi-stage causal weight placement and integer-wave compilation; no hardware changes, no performance experiment, no sealed artifacts modified.

conclusion.direct_precedent: Joint causal mapping, layout-schedule feedback, paired MLP projection partitions, and MoE expert pipelines have direct prior art. Complementary load placement is not claimed novel.
conclusion.remaining_candidate: A compiler contribution remains conditional on legally lowering exact matrix partitions to unchanged NAND dense commands, modeling native integer-wave work plus channel/host/partial-output dependencies, and beating matched geometry/readiness-aware joint controls with fixed routes and capacity.
conclusion.negative_search_is_not_exclusion: No examined section explicitly implements fixed-route MoE GU/Down NAND integer-wave high-set complement; this does not prove absence from the literature, especially the unavailable FlexLLM and DIAMoND full texts.

sources.title: PIMCOMP: An End-to-End DNN Compiler for Processing-In-Memory Accelerators
sources.venue: IEEE TCAD; extended work following DAC 2023 PIMCOMP
sources.read_depth: Read abstract and sections III-C, IV, VI-A/B, VII-A/B, Figure 7 explanation; author repository README inspected. Not a claim to have executed its compiler or read the original DAC paper in this round.
observed: Section IV-B closes the loop between layout-computation mapping and dataflow scheduling using the profiler.
Section VI-A jointly optimizes weight replication and array-group placement. Fitness runs simplified native pseudo-instruction scheduling and profiles compute, memory access, and communication.
Figure 7(d) low-latency placement puts producer and consumer array groups in the same core to avoid communication.
Section VII-B tracks pixel forward/backward and pixel-array-group dependencies and manages local memory for ready work.
sources.inference_for_current_work: An end-to-end causal layout-plus-schedule compiler is not a new category. Compare an equally budgeted readiness-aware layout search with replication disabled and the same legal geometry, rather than only per-phase fitting.
sources.hardware_boundary: Crossbar PIM template with local memory/vector functional units and backend pseudo-ISA; not evidence of AiF hardware capabilities or timings.
sources.code_evidence: Paper links author GitHub. README describes ONNX frontend, core mapping, dataflow scheduling, high-throughput/low-latency modes. Source execution was outside this audit.

sources.title: Fast-OverlaPIM: A Fast Overlap-driven Mapping Framework for Processing In-Memory Neural Network Acceleration
sources.year: 2024 preprint and author-listed TCAD publication; final issue year not independently resolved from an accessible primary publisher record in this round
sources.venue: IEEE TCAD (author homepage); preceding OverlaPIM DATE 2023
sources.read_depth: Read sections II-III, IV-B through IV-D, IV-I through IV-K, and V-A implementation, baselines, architecture configuration. Not a full-paper exhaustive review.
observed: Section IV-I sorts data spaces by input readiness and maps ready data spaces to resources using round robin, acknowledging altered partial-sum reduction movements.
Section IV-J evaluates consecutive-layer overlap during mapping search, rather than optimizing sequential layer execution then merely enabling overlap.
Section IV-K explicitly notes that a locally suboptimal predecessor mapping can produce better total performance and searches forward, backward, or from a middle layer.
Section V-A distinguishes sequentially optimized mapping evaluated with overlap, overlap-optimized mapping, and overlap-driven transformed mapping.
sources.inference_for_current_work: This is the closest direct prior against claiming joint GU/Down causal placement itself. Its baseline ladder is a useful template: same layout with improved scheduler, then joint layout under the same scheduler, then transformation.
sources.hardware_boundary: Main evaluation uses modified HBM2 majority-based bit-serial row-parallel PIM with fixed per-layer memory allocation; it is not an existing NAND command implementation.
sources.code_evidence: Section V-A says extensively customized Timeloop. No author project repository link found in the examined paper HTML or author homepage; this is not a claim that no code exists.

sources.title: Stratum: System-Hardware Co-Design with Tiered Monolithic 3D-Stackable DRAM for Efficient MoE Serving
sources.read_depth: Read sections 3.2, 4.1/Figures 8-9, 5.2, and 6.1 modeling details. No simulator execution.
observed: Section 4.1 jointly partitions the two up projections vertically and down horizontally across PUs to preserve intermediate ownership and remove inter-PU up-to-down communication.
Selected experts execute sequentially with tensor parallelism across PUs; shared input duplication is amortized across active experts.
Figure 9 overlaps the second up GEMM with activation, down reduce-scatter with the next expert's first up GEMM, and immediately aggregates expert outputs.
Within each PU, it partitions along the longer matrix dimension to improve tensor-core utilization.
sources.inference_for_current_work: A particularly close MoE prior for paired GU/Down geometry and causal expert pipelining. It does not establish that ordinary NAND wave complement is already implemented.
sources.hardware_boundary: Proposed Mono3D DRAM plus logic-die NMP includes a local special-function engine, ring network, reducers and partial-sum memory. None may be imported into AiF without independent evidence. Evaluated with device/circuit models and an in-house simulator, not a manufactured Stratum system.
sources.code_evidence: Section 6.1.2 describes an in-house simulator receiving tensor shapes, expert IDs and mappings; no public simulator link found in examined primary sections.

sources.title: Megatron-LM: Training Multi-Billion Parameter Language Models Using Model Parallelism
sources.read_depth: Read section 3 MLP derivation, equations 1-3, Figure 3 and associated all-reduce discussion; not an audit of current repository code.
observed: Column-partitions the first GEMM so nonlinearity is independently applicable, then row-partitions the second GEMM so it consumes local activation outputs without intermediate communication.
Reduces second-GEMM partial outputs across GPUs; explicitly contrasts the alternative requiring a synchronization before the nonlinearity.
sources.inference_for_current_work: Paired projection partitioning across a nonlinearity and ownership-aware TP are established. The remaining NAND question is exact native grain and causal resource cost, rather than algebraic composition.
sources.hardware_boundary: GPU dense-transformer training; no NAND page/wave model and no evidence for quantized flash return ABI.
sources.code_evidence: Official NVIDIA repository exists; current code not fetched or run in this audit.

sources.title: Cambricon-LLM: A Chiplet-Based Hybrid Architecture for On-Device Inference of 70B LLM
sources.read_depth: Read sections V-A and V-B, Figure 7 and associated equations; additionally examined source sections IV scheduling and VII-A simulator description. This is the original Cambricon-LLM, not the unavailable Cambricon-FlexLLM full text.
observed: Splits each request tile into two-dimensional page-sized atomic tiles across flash channels and compute cores.
Derives input/result movement as a function of tile aspect ratio and same-channel input broadcast, then chooses the shape minimizing movement.
Balances NPU/flash workload to consume idle channel intervals; uses a modified SSDsim and a separate NPU simulator.
sources.inference_for_current_work: Strong NAND-specific baseline for hardware-granular 2D tiling and transfer accounting. Examined sections do not give fixed-route MoE joint GU/Down wave-high placement.
sources.hardware_boundary: Dedicated flash compute/ECC and channel broadcast are that architecture's own capabilities. Shape or latency conclusions do not automatically transfer to AiF.
sources.code_evidence: Paper states modified SSDsim; no author runnable artifact verified in this round.

unavailable_full_text.title: DIAMoND: Dynamic Inference for Adaptive Edge MOE with Heterogeneous In-NAND and Near-DRAM Compute Architecture
unavailable_full_text.status: No legal author full text newly obtained. Previously read primary abstract only; no claims about detailed mapping or scheduler are made.

own_analysis.complement_does_not_reduce_work: With fixed shard sizes, permuting GU and down high sets changes queues/readiness but not total wave work. The reduction from 77 to 75 waves/expert belongs to geometry, not complement.

causal_counterexample.reason: Down waits for the complete GU result, so the pooled three-wave lower bound is unattainable despite perfect complement.

own_analysis.qwen_bound_boundary: For whole-row 3/4-wave GU and 1/2-wave down, a single expert has a six-wave GU->host->down path even if its chipwise combined load never exceeds five. Multiple expert overlap can fill gaps, so native DAG replay, not load sum alone, decides the achievable gain.
minimum_strong_controls: Use identical legal geometry candidates, single-copy weights, chip capacity, balanced labels, input reload, output transfers, host activation/reduction, shared expert geometry and native scheduler across layouts.
Include route-oblivious cyclic and complement initializations, independently phase-fitted mapping, and equally budgeted readiness-aware causal joint mapping; report seed and search-budget controls.
Separate scheduler-only improvement on a fixed mapping, geometry-only improvement on matched mappings, and additional joint placement improvement under the identical scheduler.
Report pooled useful work, per-expert critical path, chip load and channel/host-port lower bounds; do not interpret any one as achievable latency.
Test ordinary-read without CR. Keep output ABI and numerical lowering unresolved where the target architecture has not disclosed the needed contract.
potential_system_contribution_conditions: A legal native command lowering plus resource-accurate scheduler jointly selects exact wave-granular matrix geometry and fixed physical assignments across causally dependent projections.
A concise witness shows why balanced phase-local and ready-time controls fail on a real geometry, and the improvement survives their matched native replay.
The useful improvement generalizes across held-out routes/shapes or a second published backend under that backend's own native granularity, rather than importing NAND wave costs.
no_go_conditions: The new result is reproduced by a simple deterministic cyclic/complement mapping or a readiness-aware joint control with the same geometry and search budget.
Only the pooled work bound improves, while exact causal command/transfer/host replay does not.
The gain depends on free partial sums, channel broadcast, cross-plane input contexts or unpublished output formats not established on the selected backend.
